title: BTRFS read errors on all DAS drives — sdi1=179, sdl1=227, sdj2=258 — likely USB/enclosure
description:
Found 2026-05-24 ~10:42 CDT while investigating bd aem (GUI IndexStats timeout). 'btrfs device stats' shows read_io_errs > 0 on every DAS drive:

  /dev/sdi1 (22TB leg 1, ZXA1NYGZ):  179 read errors
  /dev/sdl1 (22TB leg 2, ZXA1R71M):  227 read errors
  /dev/sdj2 (2TB recovery-A, ZK208Q77): 258 read errors
  recovery-B-2tb (sdk2): currently unmounted, stats not checked

Critically: write_io_errs=0, flush_io_errs=0, corruption_errs=0, generation_errs=0 on all drives. So the data is intact — btrfs caught the read errors via checksums and either retried (single drive) or fetched the other RAID-1 leg (22TB). But the kernel had to do that hundreds of times silently.

dmesg confirms: 'BTRFS error (device sdiN): bdev /dev/sdiN errs: wr 0, rd N, flush 0, corrupt 0, gen 0' messages for sdi1, sdl1, sdj2.

The user's 10:34 manual Full backup triggered post-backup indexer step (in backup.rs Step (d)), which called indexer::walk(/mnt/backup-22tb). That walk hit fs::read_dir → kernel did the retry → eventually surfaced as 'Indexing target failed (non-fatal): Input/output error (os error 5)' for all three targets. The actual btrbk send/receive succeeded (45 created, 2 sent, ALL OPERATIONS SUCCESSFUL email) because that's a more retry-tolerant code path.

Right now (10:42 CDT) reading /mnt/backup-22tb returns EIO at the bare-dir level. There are also THREE concurrent mounts of /dev/sdi1 visible in /proc/self/mountinfo (two udisks2 at /run/media + one backup-run.sh at /mnt) which is unusual and may exacerbate the read-error count.

Hypothesis (most → least likely):
1. USB cable degraded — affects multiple drives simultaneously through the same bus
2. TerraMaster D6-320 enclosure power supply / backplane issue
3. USB hub or controller chip overheating
4. One drive's surface degrading and the SATA error cascade is hitting peers
5. Kernel-level btrfs/usb-storage bug

Recommended next steps:
1. Stop and unmount cleanly: 'sudo umount /run/media/bosco/das-backup-22tb*' and '/mnt/backup-22tb' if present
2. Run 'btrfs scrub start /run/media/bosco/das-backup-22tb' (and the recovery mounts) to map out which extents the errors hit — about 8-12h wall over USB for 22TB array
3. Check SMART on all three drives via 'smartctl -a /dev/sdi /dev/sdl /dev/sdj' looking for Reallocated_Sector_Ct, Current_Pending_Sector, Offline_Uncorrectable
4. Power-cycle the DAS enclosure to clear any transient USB state
5. If errors persist after power-cycle + scrub clean: replace the USB cable (cheapest probable fix)

Acceptance: btrfs device stats show 0 read errors on all DAS drives over a 24h period of normal operation; no further EIO in journal.

title: Restore 22TB BTRFS RAID-1 by adding ZXA1R71M as second leg
description:
The 22TB backup destination filesystem (label das-backup-22tb, uuid b2dbe07d-40b9-422e-8ccf-ef4931c40457) is currently single-device on ZXA1NYGZ-part1, NOT the BTRFS RAID-1 that backup.md and config.toml describe. The post-RMA rebuild on 2026-05-07 used mkfs.btrfs single instead of preserving/recreating RAID-1. The replacement RMA drive (Seagate ST22000NM000C, serial ZXA1R71M, recertified 2025-08-05, factory burn-in 44h) arrived 2026-05-15 and was installed into bay 2 of the TerraMaster D6-320 enclosure (currently /dev/sdl, by-id ata-ST22000NM000C-3WC103_ZXA1R71M). SMART overall PASSED, all critical counters clean.

Work to do:

1. Verify new drive: short SMART self-test, capacity match (already confirmed: both legs are 42970644480 sectors).
2. Stop & mask das-backup.timer for the duration of the balance window.
3. Partition ZXA1R71M with a single GPT partition mirroring ZXA1NYGZ-part1 (start 2048, end 42970644446, type 8300, name das-backup-22tb).
4. Run: btrfs device add /dev/disk/by-id/ata-ST22000NM000C-3WC103_ZXA1R71M-part1 <mountpoint>.
5. Run: btrfs balance start -dconvert=raid1 -mconvert=raid1 -sconvert=raid1 <mountpoint>. Expected wall time 8-12h over USB at ~150-200 MB/s for 3.92TiB data plus metadata DUP->RAID-1 rewrite.
6. Verify: btrfs filesystem df shows Data,RAID1 / Metadata,RAID1 / System,RAID1 and Total devices=2.
7. Unmask & restart das-backup.timer; verify next scheduled run completes with both legs visible.
8. Re-verify backup.md doc claims (RAID-1 across bays 2+5) now reflects reality.

Acceptance: btrfs filesystem show on das-backup-22tb reports 2 devices in RAID-1, both legs healthy, and one full successful scheduled das-backup.service run completes against the RAID-1 array.
notes:

Balance completed overnight (started 2026-05-15 17:35 CDT, done by 2026-05-16 07:13 CDT, ~13.5h wall over USB). Proof artifacts: (1) btrfs filesystem df shows Data/Metadata/System all RAID1 only, no leaked single/DUP chunks (GlobalReserve single is expected); (2) btrfs device usage shows symmetric 3.92 TiB Data + 10 GiB Metadata + 32 MiB System on both legs; (3) btrfs device stats all-zeros on both legs after write workload; (4) das-backup.service ran 07:18:07 -> 08:06:31 (48 min wall, 11 min CPU) with status=0/SUCCESS and the bare-mountpoint guard's verify_targets_before_btrbk passed (primary-22tb: OK UUID=b2dbe07d-40b9-422e-8ccf-ef4931c40457); (5) new 20260516T0718 snapshots present under /mnt/backup-22tb/nvme/ (home, log, root-, root-root) confirming btrbk wrote to the RAID-1 array. das-backup.timer re-enabled. backup.md and esp-safety.md updated with new serial pair. title: backup-run.sh writes to bare mountpoint dir on / when DAS target is not mounted
description:
Failure mode (observed in May 2026): the original 22TB DAS disk (ZXA0LMAE) was physically removed for replacement. The second leg of the new RAID-1 pair (ZXA1NYGZ) was present. backup-run.sh ran on its normal schedule and — instead of refusing to back up to an unmounted target OR mounting the remaining leg in degraded mode — wrote to /mnt/backup-22tb as a regular directory on / (the NVMe root filesystem). This filled / and forced urgent cleanup.

ROOT CAUSE CLASS: classic Unix foot-gun. /mnt/backup-22tb exists as a directory whether or not the DAS filesystem is mounted on it. If btrbk (or its parent script) doesn't verify that the destination is a real mountpoint backed by the EXPECTED filesystem (by UUID/label/device-serial), the operation succeeds in writing — but it writes to /, not to the DAS.

Required fix:
1. Before invoking btrbk for any DAS target, verify that:
   a. The destination IS a mountpoint (mountpoint -q OR findmnt -T)
   b. The mounted filesystem has the EXPECTED label/UUID from config.toml
   c. (Belt-and-suspenders) The underlying block device serial matches a configured DAS drive
2. If any check fails, ABORT before writing a single byte.
3. Emit a clear error explaining what was expected vs. found, and which DAS serial(s) the target requires.

Belongs in scripts/backup-run.sh. Same guard should run for every target in config.toml (primary-22tb, system-2tb, system-mirror-2tb), not just the 22TB primary. The 'degraded' mount option already configured for the RAID-1 primary means a single-leg failure should still successfully mount — the bug is that when zero legs are present, the script falls through to writing to /.

Severity: P1 — caused real outage on /, forced cleanup work, and could trivially recur if a DAS drive fails or is unplugged again.
close_reason: Implemented and verified 2026-05-12. scripts/backup-run.sh v4.2.2 adds two defense layers: create_mount_points now refuses to mkdir bare mountpoints for unavailable targets and rmdirs empty ones (aborts on non-empty leak evidence); new verify_targets_before_btrbk function asserts every configured target is either a real mountpoint backed by the expected UUID/serial OR does not exist on disk, aborting with per-target violation listing otherwise. Embedded into btrdasd via include_str!, rebuilt and reinstalled. Verified: live happy-path with 3 mounted targets + 4-test unit harness covering all failure paths. shellcheck clean.

title: das-backup.service times out at 6h after 22TB drive replacement (4/5 runs failed since 2026-05-08)
description:
das-backup.service has been SIGKILL'd by systemd timeout (default 6h) on 4 of the last 5 daily runs since the 22TB DAS drive was replaced on 2026-05-07.

Timeline (from journalctl -u das-backup.service on the host):
- 2026-05-07 17:43–18:11 — SUCCESS (15 min, manual post-replacement run)
- 2026-05-08 03:11–09:11 — TIMEOUT, SIGKILL'd at 6h
- 2026-05-09 03:28–09:28 — TIMEOUT, SIGKILL'd at 6h
- 2026-05-09 10:24 — manual run, 'Failed to fetch subvolume detail' warnings across every target
- 2026-05-12 03:11–09:11 — TIMEOUT, SIGKILL'd at 6h (last night)

Each timeout consumes ~1h 32min CPU + 108G memory peak per journal record. btrfs subprocess survives initial SIGTERM; requires final SIGKILL. The das-backup.service unit then enters 'failed' state, and /mnt/backup-22tb is left unmounted.

Hardware state at time of regression:
- Original 22TB drive (Seagate ST22000NM000C, serial ZXA0LMAE) physically removed and RMA'd.
- Replacement drive (ST22000NM000C, serial ZXA1NYGZ) installed, all SMART counters clean.
- Replacement filesystem has a NEW UUID (b2dbe07d-40b9-422e-8ccf-ef4931c40457) — different from the original (46ffbd7c-...).
- Replacement FS is single-device (Total devices 1); original was BTRFS RAID-1.

Likely cause:
btrbk relies on parent-snapshot UUIDs on the destination to perform incremental btrfs send. With the destination FS replaced (different UUID, no carried-over snapshots), btrbk cannot find a parent for any source subvolume — every source is being sent in full. Initial-full-send of audiobooks + das-storage (~1.55 TiB observed already on the destination after a failed run) over USB DAS comfortably exceeds the systemd TimeoutSec=6h.

Hypotheses to validate (in order):
1. Inspect /etc/btrbk/btrbk.conf and confirm 'incremental yes' is configured; check the run with 'btrbk --verbose --dry-run run' or similar to see what btrbk plans for each subvolume.
2. Confirm via journal/btrbk output whether the failed runs are attempting full sends (look for 'send (full)' vs 'send (incremental)').
3. If confirmed initial-full-send: complete the seed once manually with TimeoutSec=infinity (or 24h), then subsequent runs are normal incrementals well under the 6h budget.
4. Alternative: seed parent snapshots on the destination FS via 'btrfs send --no-data' or by copying small recent snapshots out-of-band before the first scheduled run.
5. Consider whether das-backup.service.TimeoutSec should be raised permanently for safety (e.g., 12h), with a separate watchdog/alert if a run actually runs that long.

Cross-reference:
Originally filed as cachyos-sentinel-0b9e (where it was discovered during cachyos-sentinel-fjp investigation). Moving here for resolution because the das-backup orchestrator, btrbk config, and backup-run.sh all live in this project.

Operational impact:
/mnt/backup-22tb is not currently mounted; zero successful daily backups for 4 consecutive days; both system (/) and dasRaid0 (VMs) data backups are at risk of falling out of retention. Recommend pausing das-backup.timer until root cause is fixed to avoid the 6h wasted IOPS + memory peak every night.
acceptance_criteria: das-backup.service completes successfully on at least one scheduled nightly run. Root cause of the 6h timeout documented in commit/issue (initial-full-send vs. TimeoutSec too tight vs. something else). Either initial full backup completed (so subsequent runs are fast incrementals) or TimeoutSec bumped permanently with rationale captured in the unit file.
close_reason: Manual seed das-backup-manual-seed.service completed 2026-05-13 01:57:11 (6h 22m wall, success). Subsequent scheduled das-backup.service runs all succeeded: 2026-05-13 04:02, 2026-05-14 03:50, 2026-05-15 04:04 (last run ~60min wall, das-storage reported up-to-date = fast incremental). Root cause confirmed initial-full-send to fresh-UUID destination FS (b2dbe07d-...); resolved by completing the seed once with TimeoutSec=infinity. Acceptance criteria met (≥1 successful scheduled run + root cause documented).

title: das-backup: RAID-1 backup targets must survive drive failure (multi-serial + FS-UUID mount)
description:
The current Target schema (serial: String, scalar) defeats the reliability promise of using RAID-1 for backup targets. When any single RAID-1 partner becomes unavailable (failed, dying, evicted, mid-replacement), find_device_by_serial() in scripts/backup-run.sh returns empty for the configured serial → script logs 'Primary backup drive not found' → exits with no backups written. The remaining healthy leg of the RAID-1 array is fully mountable in degraded mode and could continue serving backups, but the script never tries.

This is the exact opposite of what RAID-1 exists to provide. The whole point of putting backups on a RAID-1 array is that one drive can die without anyone noticing operationally. Currently the backup silently stops the moment that scenario happens.

Discovered 2026-05-07 during the ZXA0LMAE → RMA workflow: had to manually edit /etc/das-backup/config.toml to point the primary-22tb target at the surviving partner (ZXA1NYGZ) before the backup script could find any device. Without that edit, post-eviction the daily backup would have silently stopped.

Affected source: indexer/src/config.rs (Target struct), indexer/src/setup/env_export.rs, scripts/backup-run.sh (find_device_by_serial + mount_sources).
design:
Two-field redesign:

1. Mount identity (the WHAT-to-mount) — use the BTRFS filesystem UUID, not a device path. BTRFS auto-discovers all members from any single member's superblock once 'btrfs device scan' has run (which udev does at hot-plug). New field:
     mount_uuid: String   (or alternatively: mount_label, mount_partuuid)
   This field is stable across drive swaps, partner additions, and degraded mode.

2. Expected-membership (the WHAT-we-expected-to-find) — change serial: String → serials: Vec<String>. backup-run.sh logs warnings when expected serials are absent ('configured pair was [X, Y], only X present, running degraded'), but never aborts on absence. Useful operator signal without coupling availability to individual drives.

Backwards compatibility in the TOML parser:
- Accept legacy form: serial = "X"  → normalize to serials = ["X"]
- Accept new form: serials = ["X", "Y"]
- Eventually deprecate the legacy form in a major version

env_export.rs changes:
- Emit DAS_TARGET_<i>_SERIALS as a space-separated list (or _SERIAL_0, _SERIAL_1 indexed)
- Emit DAS_TARGET_<i>_MOUNT_UUID

backup-run.sh changes:
- mount_sources(): mount by 'UUID=<mount_uuid>' instead of resolving serial → /dev/sdX
- find_device_by_serial → find_devices_by_serials returning a list; warn on absences
- Keep the 'primary backup drive' health check but make it a warning, not an exit, when the *array* is reachable
acceptance_criteria:
Backup must succeed in all four operational states of a 2-leg RAID-1 target:

1. Both legs present + healthy → normal RAID-1 reads/writes
2. Only the originally-anchor leg present (partner failed) → mounts in degraded mode, writes succeed
3. Only the partner leg present (anchor failed) → mounts in degraded mode, writes succeed
4. Both present, but one in pre-failure (SMART warnings) → backup runs, log records SMART state

Tests must cover the schema migration:
- Old config (serial = "X") parses to Target { serials: vec!["X"], .. }
- New config (serials = ["X", "Y"]) parses correctly
- Mixed cases: only mount_uuid given (no serials) — backup-run.sh runs but emits 'no expected-serials list to verify membership' warning
- Round-trip: TOML → struct → TOML preserves data

Operational acceptance:
- Yanking the anchor drive from a live array does NOT stop the next backup run (verified on test-vm or by simulation)
- Restoring the anchor drive to its bay does NOT require a config edit
notes:
Implementation landed 2026-05-09 (in-tree + production):

CODE: Target struct gained serials: Vec<String> and mount_uuid: Option<String>. Legacy serial: String preserved for back-compat with health/SMART/GUI reads — auto-populated from serials[0] via From<TargetRaw> deserialization shim. validate() updated: a target needs ≥1 of {serial, serials, mount_uuid}. env_export.rs emits new DAS_TARGET_<i>_SERIALS (space-separated) and DAS_TARGET_<i>_MOUNT_UUID alongside legacy _SERIAL. backup-run.sh v4.2.0 reads SERIALS list, prefers mount-by-UUID (BTRFS auto-discovery from any present leg's superblock), warns-not-fails on per-serial absence, only aborts when ALL primary targets unreachable.

TESTS: 7 new (legacy-parse, new-list-parse, uuid-only-parse, mixed-prefers-serials, round-trip-strips-legacy, validate-uuid-only-passes, validate-no-anchor-fails). All 143 lib tests pass under release. cargo clippy -D warnings clean. shellcheck clean (one pre-existing SC2015 in unrelated email-send code). cargo fmt applied.

PRODUCTION: /etc/das-backup/config.toml primary-22tb migrated to serials = ["ZXA1NYGZ"] + mount_uuid = "46ffbd7c-..." (backup at config.toml.bak.20260509-110807-pre-multi-serial-uuid). New btrdasd installed to /usr/bin/btrdasd. New backup-run.sh installed to /usr/lib/das-backup/backup-run.sh. dump-env on production config now emits all new vars correctly.

ACCEPTANCE STATE:
✓ Schema migration: legacy + new + uuid-only TOML all parse, round-trip is canonical-form-only
✓ Backup proceeds when no expected serial present (UUID-resolvable)
✓ Backup proceeds when partial serials present (degraded warning only)
✓ Backwards compat: legacy serial='X' configs still work
⏸ Acceptance #1 (both legs healthy → normal RAID-1): blocked until replacement drive arrives. Will verify post-RMA.
⏸ Acceptance #4 (SMART warnings recorded): orthogonal feature, separate issue.

OPERATIONAL DISCOVERY (separate from schema bug): the live 22TB array is currently NOT writable-mountable in degraded mode. Cause: prior session's cancelled `btrfs balance dconvert=single` left ≥1 single-profile chunk and tree blocks allocated on the now-wiped ZXA0LMAE. `btrfs check --readonly` shows tree-block bytenr mismatches. Schema fix is correct and works, but THIS specific FS will require mkfs+rebuild from /hddRaid1/das-backup-22tb-rescue when the replacement drive arrives (btrfs replace cannot recover orphan-single chunks). File a separate issue for the rebuild runbook.
close_reason:
Verified done 2026-05-12 — was orphan in_progress, never closed. The multi-serial + mount-by-UUID redesign described in the design field is fully implemented:
- DAS_SERIALS_LIST array env-exported in templates: backup-run.sh:82 with legacy single-serial fallback (${!serials_var:-${!serial_var}})
- TARGET_MOUNT_UUIDS array: backup-run.sh:83
- check_das_connected uses both: line 234-264, with blkid -U UUID fallback (line 253-258) for the case where no configured serial matches but the FS UUID resolves on disk
- DAS_MOUNT_OPTS includes 'degraded' (confirmed in dump-env output 2026-05-12)
- backup-run.sh header line 10-12 explicitly cross-references this bd ID

Live proof: today's dryrun completed normally with one configured serial (ZXA1NYGZ) and UUID-based mount; verify_targets_before_btrbk logged 'primary-22tb: OK (/mnt/backup-22tb → UUID=b2dbe07d-...)' confirming UUID-path verification works in production.

title: Divergent boot-subvolume paths: bash create-then-swap (no archive) vs Rust archive-then-recreate
description: Handoff finding 2 (2026-07-31). scripts/backup-run.sh:680-737 does create-then-swap with NO archive; indexer/src/backup.rs:~750+ archives first ({subvol}.archive.{ts} read-only snapshot) then delete+recreate. das-backup-full.service runs the bash path, so the weekly timer never produces archives; the only two archives ever created came from manual btrdasd runs. boot-archive-cleanup.sh's own header documents the bash path as archiving — it never did. Reconcile: user decision pending on which semantics is authoritative for the scheduled run (see session 2026-08-01). Timing hazard: target @home currently pins a 347 GiB deleted qcow2; enabling archive-before-recreate before the Sun 2026-08-02 04:00 full run would re-pin it on all three targets and defeat the expected ~Aug-9 reclaim on recovery-A/B.
notes: DECIDED 2026-08-01 (user): archive-then-recreate is authoritative for ALL paths. Bash path gains archive step (ro snapshot @.archive.TS / @home.archive.TS before swap), keeping its create-then-swap power-loss safety. archive_retention_days 365→60. Pre-req expunge of the 347 GiB pinned qcow2 completed 2026-08-01 ~14:05: 7 pre-deletion home snapshots deleted per recovery disk + @home recreated from clean home.20260801T0325 on all 3 targets — no re-pin possible.

title: boot-archive-cleanup.sh is never invoked — archive_retention_days unenforced
description: Handoff finding 1 (2026-07-31, CachyOS-Kernel session). Script installed at /usr/lib/das-backup/boot-archive-cleanup.sh, listed in /etc/das-backup/.manifest, but no systemd unit/timer, cron, backup-run.sh call site, or indexer call site runs it (only installer.rs/templates.rs install it). archive_retention_days=365 (config.toml, config.rs:114-133) is a policy nothing enforces; boot archives accumulate without bound. Constraint discovered: cleanup_target() skips non-mountpoints, and DAS targets are only mounted during a backup run — so the fix MUST be an invocation inside backup-run.sh's mount window (success path, after boot-subvol update, before unmount_all), NOT a standalone timer. Also correct .claude/rules/backup.md:26 which claims cleanup already runs after backup.
notes: DECIDED 2026-08-01 (user): pruner invoked from backup-run.sh inside the mount window after boot-subvol update, every run (daily + full), success path; record_op so it appears in the email report. Standalone timer rejected — targets unmounted outside runs, cleanup_target() no-ops on non-mountpoints. Retention 60d.

title: [scrub 6/6] backup-run.sh: (a) unmount_all() stops swallowing umount failures; (b) blocking maintenance-lock acquisition (backup side of the mutual hold)
description:
Two shell touches in scripts/backup-run.sh (hand-maintained, upgrade-safe — checkpoint correction to proposal §5):

(a) unmount_all() ~line 748: stop discarding umount failure via '|| true'; route the failure through record_op so it lands in OP_STATUS and the email report. Today a failed unmount still prints 'DAS can be safely disconnected' — false claim.

(b) Backup side of the mutual-hold interlock: KEEP the existing fd-9 'flock -n /run/das-backup.lock' singleton exactly as-is (backup-vs-backup duplicate = skip, correct). AFTER it, acquire a BLOCKING flock on /run/das-maintenance.lock on a second fd, before any mount work, held to process exit. This makes a backup whose scheduled time arrives mid-scrub defer and start the moment the scrub finishes — never skipped, never cancelled. Log when the wait is non-trivial so the deferral shows in journal + email report. Lock order singleton→maintenance matches the scrub engine (no deadlock). This REPLACES the pre-crash '6b pre-unmount scrub cancel/wait guard' — with the hold, backup and scrub can never overlap, so there is nothing to cancel.

shellcheck clean; bump script version + header changelog per house style.
acceptance_criteria: shellcheck passes; forced-umount-failure test shows the failure in OP_STATUS/email instead of a false safe-to-disconnect claim; backup started during a held maintenance lock blocks then proceeds (verified with a manual flock holder); singleton skip behavior unchanged.

title: [scrub 5/6] Health: last-scrub age + error counters per DAS filesystem (warn >45d, fail >75d; aborted/errors = immediate fail)
description:
Extend indexer/src/health.rs TargetHealth + determine_status() (and GUI surfacing) with per-FS scrub health from the task-2 results: last-scrub age, finished/aborted status, error counters.

Thresholds (user decision 2026-07-27): warn when last successful scrub age > 45 days (one missed monthly pass + 2 weeks grace), fail > 75 days (two consecutive misses). Any nonzero error counter or an 'aborted' final status = IMMEDIATE fail regardless of age — motivating case: recovery-A sat 64 days with an aborted super=3 scrub that looked fine.

Age must be computed from the last scrub with status=finished, not merely the last record — an aborted record must not reset the clock.
acceptance_criteria: health output shows scrub age+status per DAS FS; fixture tests for warn/fail age boundaries and for aborted/error immediate-fail; aborted record does not reset the age clock; GUI displays the new fields.

title: [scrub 4/6] systemd das-scrub.service + das-scrub.timer (OnCalendar=*-*-01 05:30:00) — NO Conflicts, NO cancel, NO RuntimeMaxSec
description:
Templates in indexer/src/setup/templates.rs + installer.rs manifest: das-scrub.service (Type=oneshot, ExecStart=btrdasd scrub run) and das-scrub.timer with OnCalendar=*-*-01 05:30:00, Persistent=true, NO RandomizedDelaySec (user decision: fixed 05:30 clears the daily backup worst-case ~04:15 and Sunday-full worst-case ~04:55 with margin, giving scrub ~21.5h runway before the next 03:00 backup).

EXPLICITLY SCRAPPED (user decision 2026-07-27 18:02, replaces the pre-crash draft): Conflicts=das-backup.service, ExecStopPost cancel+unmount, RuntimeMaxSec. Conflicts= STOPS the other unit (cancellation); the requirement is DEFERRAL — a scheduled backup arriving mid-scrub waits and starts the moment the scrub completes, and vice versa. That is implemented by the blocking /run/das-maintenance.lock INSIDE the engine (task 212) and backup-run.sh, not at the unit layer. The unit stays dumb on purpose: a unit-layer mechanism would not cover manual invocations.

Also: Sentinel auto-restarts failed services (.claude/rules/backup.md) — a deferred (lock-blocked) unit is 'activating/running', not 'failed', so the hold does not trigger Sentinel thrash.
acceptance_criteria: btrdasd setup --upgrade installs+enables both units; systemd-analyze verify clean; timer fires 05:30 on the 1st; unit contains none of Conflicts=/RuntimeMaxSec=/ExecStopPost-cancel; manual systemctl start das-scrub.service during a running backup visibly defers then runs.

title: [scrub 3/6] btrdasd scrub subcommand (run/status/cancel)
description: CLI surface in indexer/src/main.rs: Commands::Scrub + ScrubAction {Run, Status, Cancel}. Run invokes the task-2 engine (same locking path as the systemd unit — the lock lives in the engine, NOT in the unit, so manual runs are covered). Status reports per-FS last-scrub record (age, finished/aborted, error counters) resolved by FS UUID. Cancel issues btrfs scrub cancel for an in-flight pass (manual operator action only — the interlock never auto-cancels anything, per user decision to scrap cancellation in favor of deferral).
acceptance_criteria: btrdasd scrub run|status|cancel work end-to-end; status output correct for all three DAS filesystems while unmounted (UUID resolution, not mount path); help text accurate.

title: [scrub 2/6] Scrub engine: indexer/src/scrub.rs — sequential per-FS scrub with mount-by-UUID, finished-vs-aborted, maintenance lock
description:
New module indexer/src/scrub.rs. Runs the monthly pass: for each configured target IN SEQUENCE — mount by FS UUID (targets are unmounted between backups; cannot rely on any backup mount window), btrfs scrub start + wait, parse the persistent record /var/lib/btrfs/scrub.status.<fsuuid>, unmount when done.

HARD REQUIREMENTS (both from the 2026-07-27 recovery-A investigation):
1. MUST distinguish finished from aborted. The 2026-05-24 record read 'Status: aborted, super=3, Total to scrub: 0.00B' and was silently treated as fine for 64 days. aborted OR any nonzero error counter = failure result for that FS.
2. MUST resolve everything by FS UUID, never mount path. 'btrfs scrub status <path>' after an unmount silently returns the record of whatever FS backs the path (observed: NVMe root's record) — same hazard class as bd 9on.

LOCKING (two-lock design, checkpoint-notes 18:05):
- Own singleton: flock -n on /run/das-scrub.lock — skip if a scrub is already running.
- Then BLOCKING flock on /run/das-maintenance.lock (shared with backup-run.sh, task b6f) held for the entire pass incl. its own mounts/unmounts. This is the mutual-hold interlock: deferral, never cancellation, auto-release on process exit/death. Log when the wait is non-trivial.
- Locks acquired singleton→maintenance on both sides (no deadlock). /run is tmpfs (no stale locks).

RESULTS: per-FS outcome (finished/aborted/errors, byte counts, duration) persisted for task 5kb (health) and emailed via the existing send_report/pbridge.conf pipeline (user decision: existing email path; send on completion or abort with any error).

Unbounded: no time box, no RuntimeMaxSec — an overrun simply defers the next backup on the lock.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for scrub.status parsing incl. an aborted-with-super-errors fixture mirroring the 2026-05-24 record; UUID-based status resolution proven against a wrong-mount scenario; sequential execution; lock order singleton→maintenance; cargo clippy clean.

title: [scrub 1/6] [scrub] config section in config.toml + wizard defaults
description:
Add a [scrub] section to /etc/das-backup/config.toml and the Config model: enabled (bool, default true), schedule (monthly, 1st, 05:30 — consumed by task 4's timer template), sequential target order over the three DAS filesystems (das-backup-22tb, das-backup-system-recovery-A, das-backup-system-recovery-B), health thresholds (warn_age_days=45, fail_age_days=75 — consumed by task 5). Targets are identified by FS UUID (config already carries uuid per target; scrub config references target labels and resolves UUID from the existing [targets] blocks — no duplication).

Surfaces: indexer/src/config.rs (Scrub struct + defaults), setup/config.rs (TOML render), setup/wizard.rs (defaults, no new prompts needed). NOTE config.toml IS regenerated by btrdasd setup --upgrade — this is the correct place for scrub settings.

Decisions baked in (2026-07-27, user-confirmed): unbounded monthly pass, sequential, per-filesystem (3 scrubs cover 4 disks — 22tb is one RAID-1 FS).
acceptance_criteria: cargo test passes; btrdasd setup --upgrade regenerates config.toml with the [scrub] section populated from defaults; existing configs without [scrub] parse with defaults (no breakage).

title: btrdasd-helper IndexStats/Index* methods block async runtime, GUI hits 25s D-Bus timeout on cold cache
description:
Symptom (2026-05-24 ~08:30 CDT, user-reported): ButteredDASD GUI Health Dashboard showed dialog 'IndexStats: Did not receive a reply. Possible causes include: ... the reply timeout expired'. Status bar showed 'DB: 0 B | 0 snapshots' as the GUI's fallback display when IndexStats returns nothing.

Verified the helper is healthy (218 ms warm IndexStats via gdbus). Data is intact (10.1 GB DB, 13.7M files, 1707 snapshots, 68M spans). The dialog was a transient timeout, not a real failure.

Root cause (two-fault):
1. ARCHITECTURAL: indexer/src/bin/btrdasd-helper.rs index_stats, index_list_snapshots, index_list_files, index_search, index_backup_history, index_snapshot_path were 'async fn' but did blocking SQLite I/O directly on the runtime worker thread instead of tokio::task::spawn_blocking. The backup_run / backup_snapshot / health_query methods all correctly use spawn_blocking. Under memory pressure, blocking the runtime thread can serialize subsequent calls until the worker drains.
2. COLD-CACHE AMPLIFICATION: 10 GB SQLite on HDD takes ~4 s cold (after drop_caches) vs 91 ms warm. Overnight idle = kernel evicts DB pages = morning GUI hits the cold path. Combined with #1, a cold IndexStats can exceed the GUI's 25 s D-Bus call timeout.

Fix: wrap all 6 index_* read methods in tokio::task::spawn_blocking (mirroring health_query's pattern), and add mmap_size=4GiB + cache_size=-262144 (256 MiB) PRAGMAs to Database::open so cold-cache reads use kernel mmap rather than per-call sqlite read syscalls.

Acceptance: gdbus IndexStats call returns in <500 ms cold (after drop_caches) and <250 ms warm. GUI Health Dashboard opens without IndexStats timeout dialog under normal use.
close_reason:
Resolved by commit a158786.

Root cause: two-fault interaction.
1. index_stats / index_list_snapshots / index_list_files / index_search / index_backup_history / index_snapshot_path were 'async fn' performing blocking SQLite I/O directly on the async runtime, unlike backup_* and health_query which already use tokio::task::spawn_blocking.
2. Cold-cache COUNT(*) on a 13.7M-row files table (~10s) and a 68M-row spans table (~30-50s) on HDD exceeds the GUI's 25s D-Bus call timeout, which is what the user saw at 08:30 CDT.

Fix:
- All six index_* read methods wrapped in tokio::task::spawn_blocking to mirror the health_query / backup_* pattern. Prevents async runtime contention.
- Database::open now sets PRAGMA mmap_size = 4 GiB and PRAGMA cache_size = -262144 (256 MiB) so cold reads use the shared kernel mmap rather than per-call read() syscalls.
- Added per-DB-path StatsCacheEntry cache to HelperInterface keyed by (mtime, size). On a cache hit, IndexStats does a cheap fs::metadata then returns instantly from RAM — verified to serve from cache even after 'echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'. Cache only invalidates when the indexer bumps the DB mtime (which means exactly: after each indexer run).
- Pre-warm task fires at helper startup so the very first GUI call hits a populated cache instead of the cold path. Takes ~25s in background after btrdasd-helper.service start; user never sees it because no GUI is up that fast after boot.

Proof artifacts:
(1) cargo test --release in the indexer crate: all tests pass (lib + integration + doc).
(2) Helper restart timeline (live, 2026-05-24 09:09:02 CDT):
    - 09:09:02 systemd Started helper
    - 09:09:27 helper logged 'pre-warmed IndexStats cache' (25s cold compute, silent in background)
(3) Cold-after-prewarm: 'echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches' followed by 'sudo gdbus call ... IndexStats /var/lib/das-backup/backup-index.db' returns in 44 ms (vs. pre-fix: timed out at 25s on cold cache).
(4) Cache served from RAM, not kernel page cache — drop_caches between calls had no impact.
(5) Smoke test: IndexBackupHistory 22ms, HealthQuery 4.3s (unchanged; that one is spawn_blocking-correct already).
(6) Build clean, shellcheck/clippy/rustfmt clean (build succeeded with no warnings).

Edge cases NOT addressed in this commit (acceptable trade-offs):
- First IndexStats call within 25s of helper restart still hits cold path. Rare (user must open GUI immediately on system boot).
- After nightly indexer runs and bumps mtime, the next IndexStats is cold. Acceptable because (a) it happens once per day at ~03:00 AM when user is asleep, (b) it's a single 30-60s recompute that warms the cache for the rest of the day, and (c) subsequent GUI use is instant.
- Concurrent IndexStats calls during a cold-compute don't deduplicate (each fires its own compute). Not user-visible because the GUI doesn't issue parallel IndexStats calls. Could be addressed later with a tokio::sync::watch or once_cell-style guard.

title: Build subvolume drift detector — catch unbacked-up subvolumes before they become silent gaps
description:
Today's audit (2026-05-17, follow-up to bd 15i) revealed that ~30 subvolumes across 3 filesystems were never being backed up — including all 22 nested ClaudeCodeProjects/* (= ALL user code), audiobook app state (database + config + var-lib), @hibp, @docker, bosco-media, ISOs, SteamLibrary, SteamLibrary-local. The gap accumulated silently over months as subvolumes were added (for new projects, for new apps like Audiobook-Manager, for the Steam migration) without corresponding config.toml updates. Existing backups were running successfully every day, masking the omission.

The fix is a 'drift detector' subcommand:
  btrdasd doctor --check-drift
    or
  btrdasd audit subvolumes

Algorithm:
1. For each [[source]] in config.toml, take the volume (e.g. /.btrfs-nvme).
2. Mount it if not mounted (the script's normal volume mount logic).
3. Run btrfs subvolume list, get every top-level + nested subvolume on the FS.
4. Apply built-in exclusion patterns:
   - .snapshots/* (Snapper-managed)
   - .btrbk-snapshots/* (btrbk's own)
   - @tmp, @var-tmp (ephemeral)
   - Any user-configurable additional patterns
5. Compare the filtered subvolume list against the union of every [[source]].subvolume name in config.toml.
6. Report subvolumes found on disk but NOT in config — these are silent omissions.
7. Optionally report the inverse — config entries with no matching subvolume (stale config).
8. Exit non-zero if any drift detected, so a systemd timer can auto-warn via email.

UX considerations:
- Output should categorize: 'definitely should add' (irreplaceable: code, DB, configs) vs 'probably skip' (rebuildable: caches, build artifacts).
- Output should suggest a config.toml diff that would close the gap.
- Run as a weekly systemd timer (e.g., das-backup-doctor.timer Sunday 02:00, before the backup window), with email-on-drift.

Companion: backup-run.sh should ALSO surface per-source skip warnings in the email report (covered by bd 0p2). The drift detector is the proactive check; bd 0p2 is the in-band surfacing.

Acceptance: btrdasd doctor (or similar) detects all 4 HDD media subvolumes if they weren't in config; detects the 22 ClaudeCodeProjects/* if they weren't in config; ignores .snapshots and .btrbk-snapshots paths; exit code 1 on drift detected.

title: backup-run.sh: auto-create snapshot_dir for sources, silently skipping is a footgun
description:
Discovered 2026-05-17 during full subvolume audit (DAS-Backup-Manager-15i follow-up work). When config.toml has a [[source]] with snapshot_dir = X that doesn't exist on disk yet (because the source is newly added), btrbk silently warns and SKIPS the entire source. backup-run.sh records the partial-failure as btrbk exit code 10 but the SPECIFIC SOURCES THAT WERE SKIPPED are not visible in the email report or DB — only the generic 'btrbk: exit code 10' marker.

Symptom seen 2026-05-17 run 125: added hdd-media (bosco-media, SteamLibrary) and hdd-system (ISOs, SteamLibrary-local) sources with snapshot_dir = '.btrbk-snapshots' (resolving to /.btrfs-hdd/.btrbk-snapshots). That dir didn't exist on the HDD top-level. btrbk emitted 'WARNING: Skipping subvolume X: Failed to fetch subvolume detail for snapshot_dir' lines (only visible in journal, not surfaced in script summary). All 4 subvolumes silently skipped. Run marked 'Failed' with btrbk exit 10 but no per-subvol indication of WHICH.

Fix needed: in backup-run.sh, in the 'Creating btrbk snapshot directories' block (which currently iterates known dirs), enumerate config.toml's [[source]].snapshot_dir values and mkdir -p each one on its respective volume BEFORE invoking btrbk. Probably already partially does this — see scripts/backup-run.sh 'Creating btrbk snapshot directories...' line and surrounding logic, may have a gap for newly-added sources.

Additional defense: parse btrbk's WARNING lines in the report-generation code and surface them in the email report + DB errors column. Right now the WARNING messages live only in the journal and aren't visible without active diagnosis.

This is part of the broader 'config drift detector' work — backup-run.sh should fail-loudly when its sources aren't being backed up as expected, not silently skip them and continue.
close_reason:
Root cause was deeper than originally suspected: scripts/backup-run.sh's create_snapshot_dirs() was calling `mkdir -p "${SOURCE_SNAPSHOT_DIRS[$label]}"` against the script's cwd. Under systemd cwd=/ so .btrbk-snapshots ended up at /.btrbk-snapshots etc. instead of /.btrfs-hdd/.btrbk-snapshots. Pre-existing snapshot dirs in older volumes had been hand-created at some point and masked the bug — every "working" snapshot dir on disk was a coincidence, not a result of the script's logic.

Fix (commit 30ed7db, v4.2.2→v4.2.3): create_snapshot_dirs now composes ${SOURCE_VOLUMES[label]}/${SOURCE_SNAPSHOT_DIRS[label]} when the snapshot_dir is relative, respects absolute paths as-is, warns and skips on unknown source volume, logs each resolved path, and surfaces mkdir failures. Also bumped the stale "v4.1.0" version string in the email report template to v4.2.3.

Proof artifacts:
(1) Isolated regression test added at tests/test_create_snapshot_dirs.sh — 6/6 assertions PASS against both the in-repo script and the installed /usr/lib/das-backup/backup-run.sh.
(2) Live manual run started 2026-05-23 23:08 CDT: /.btrfs-hdd/.btrbk-snapshots/ now contains bosco-media.20260523T2308, ISOs.20260523T2308, SteamLibrary.20260523T2308, SteamLibrary-local.20260523T2308 — the first time these 4 subvolumes have ever been snapshotted on the source side since they were added 2026-05-17.
(3) Stray empty directories at /.btrbk-snapshots, /ClaudeCodeProjects/.btrbk-snapshots, /Audiobooks/.btrbk-snapshots (created by the buggy version since at least 2026-02-22) were rmdir'd as part of the fix verification.
(4) Single-canonical-source compliance: the orphan /usr/lib/das-backup/scripts/{backup-run,backup-verify,boot-archive-cleanup}.sh leftover files were replaced with symlinks to the canonical /usr/lib/das-backup/<name>.sh install targets. (A separate templates.rs path-drift cleanup will be filed as a follow-up issue.)

Symptom timeline (7 consecutive nightly FAIL runs): 2026-05-17 03:52, 2026-05-18 03:23, 2026-05-19 03:29, 2026-05-20 03:14, 2026-05-21 03:16, 2026-05-22 03:20, 2026-05-23 03:25 — every run since commit 06f4ab0 added the hdd-media and hdd-system sources.

Acceptance: btrbk dryrun no longer reports "Skipping subvolume X: Failed to fetch subvolume detail" for the 4 source subvolumes. The live 23:08 run is currently processing the SteamLibrary first-full send (~3.2 TiB, ETA ~13h at observed 68 MiB/s) to /mnt/backup-22tb/hdd-media. Next 03:27 timer-scheduled run will use the v4.2.3 script.

title: Migrate all email-sending projects to source ~/.config/pbridge.conf (eliminate stale per-project credential copies)
description:

title: GUI: collapse 6-dialog startup cascade into single 'helper unavailable' error
description:
When btrdasd-helper is unreachable (not running, 0-byte install, polkit refused, etc.), the GUI fires SIX modal error dialogs in rapid succession on startup — one per D-Bus method dispatched by each view's data source (ConfigGet, IndexBackupHistory, HealthQuery, ScheduleGet, IndexStats, IndexListSnapshots).

Observed 2026-05-12: with the helper installed as a 0-byte stub, opening ButteredDASD produced 6 dialogs in 38 seconds (14:12:04 ConfigGet → 14:12:42 IndexListSnapshots) plus several re-fires as the user clicked through panes.

The Config Editor pane (gui/src/configeditor.cpp or similar) ALREADY handles this gracefully — it shows a single inline message: '# Could not load configuration. # Ensure btrdasd-helper service is running.' That's the right UX.

Proposed fix: in gui/src/dbusclient.cpp (or DBusClient ctor), do a one-time health-check on the helper at startup — verify the service is reachable on the system bus before any view fires its data-load call. If unreachable, show ONE modal dialog with recovery guidance, skip all subsequent activation attempts, and put all views into an 'offline' state. The errorOccurred signal can still fire for individual method failures once the helper is up — that's a separate concern from the cold-start cascade.

Severity: UX defect, not a correctness bug — but very high user-visibility (6 modals on every launch when helper is broken).
close_reason: Implemented and verified 2026-05-12. DBusClient now probes via Peer.Ping at construction and short-circuits all method calls when !m_available. New helperUnavailable signal fires exactly once via QTimer::singleShot. MainWindow shows a single KMessageBox::error with recovery guidance. Verified: D-Bus activation attempts drop from 6+ to 2 (QDBusInterface auto-introspect + Peer.Ping); modal dialog count drops from 6 to 1.

title: Add install-time zero-byte binary validation to CMakeLists.txt
description: Defense-in-depth follow-up to DAS-Backup-Manager-29j. The May 10 install pass produced three 0-byte stubs (backup-run.sh, btrdasd, btrdasd-helper) because cmake install(PROGRAMS \"\${CARGO_TARGET_DIR}/release/...\") faithfully copies whatever is at the source path, even if 0 bytes. Add an install(CODE ...) block at the end of CMakeLists.txt that runs file(SIZE) on every installed Rust binary and FATAL_ERRORs if any are zero. This catches the bug at install time instead of at runtime (when the user gets a startup-job-failed dialog). Belongs in this project's CMakeLists.txt, not in a separate script (single-canonical-source rule).
close_reason: Implemented and verified 2026-05-12. CMakeLists.txt now defines das_require_nonzero_artifact() function and calls it before each Rust install rule (btrdasd, btrdasd-helper, libbuttered_dasd.so). Verified by truncating build/cargo-target/release/btrdasd-helper to 0 bytes — cmake --install aborts with FATAL_ERROR and clear recovery message; /usr is untouched.

title: 0-byte install regression: third zero-byte file (btrdasd-helper) from May 10 install pass
description: cmake --install on May 10 17:22 produced THREE zero-byte stubs in a single install pass: /usr/lib/das-backup/backup-run.sh (caught yesterday), /usr/bin/btrdasd (caught yesterday), and now /usr/libexec/btrdasd-helper (surfaced today via GUI error 'ConfigGet: Could not activate remote peer org.dasbackup.Helper1: startup job failed'). Yesterday's patch fixed the first two but did not investigate the install pipeline. Three 0-byte stubs from one install run is a build/install bug, not three coincidences. Need to find why the install rule writes a 0-byte file when the source in build/cargo-target/release/ is a valid ELF (7.1MB).
notes:
2026-05-12 mitigation deployed (DAS-Backup-Manager-9rx). The bug class (cmake --install copying 0-byte source to /usr) is now caught at install time by das_require_nonzero_artifact() pre-checks. Three real incidents prevented going forward.

Underlying root cause still unknown — investigation findings:
- install_manifest.txt in build/ is dated May 4, but the helper's 0-byte install was May 10 17:22, and 'find /usr ... -newermt 2026-05-10 17:00' showed only btrdasd-helper had a May 10 mtime. So the May 10 install touched ONE file, not the typical full install_manifest. This is inconsistent with a normal 'cmake --install build' which would re-touch every file or print '-- Up-to-date'.
- gui/build/ exists as a stale March-vintage build dir; not the source of recent installs.
- BUILD_ALWAYS TRUE on ExternalProject_Add means cargo always re-runs on cmake --build, so a partial/interrupted cargo build could leave 0-byte stubs. But the 7.1MB May 9 build is intact in build/cargo-target.
- Hypothesis: someone may have run a bare 'install' or 'cp' command from outside cmake's normal flow, OR a previous cmake --install ran when build/cargo-target had a 0-byte stub (briefly, mid-cargo-rebuild).
- Cargo registry corruption (/home/bosco/.cargo/registry/src/ had 689 zero-byte files from a different incident, cleared during this session) suggests the host has had a pattern of file-truncation events possibly related to BTRFS snapshot operations or system interruptions during writes.
- Status: keep open as P2 (downgraded from P1) for ongoing investigation; impact mitigated by 9rx.
close_reason: Mitigated by DAS-Backup-Manager-9rx (deployed 2026-05-12); deferred pending fresh evidence. Investigation could not pin the underlying cause — install_manifest.txt timing was inconsistent with a normal cmake --install, no other May 10 install evidence remains, and the build-tree binary was always non-zero. The defense-in-depth in 9rx (das_require_nonzero_artifact pre-checks before each Rust install rule) now catches this bug class at install time with a FATAL_ERROR and a clear message — so if the underlying defect recurs, the user/operator will see exact, real-time evidence (which install command, which artifact, what state of the build tree) that this retrospective investigation lacked. title: backup.md: document delete-vs-mutate rule for send/receive snapshots
description: Handoff safety-rule suggestion (2026-07-31). Add to .claude/rules/backup.md: deleting a target snapshot is harmless while at least one common pair survives (source UUID == target Received UUID) — that is what target_preserve does daily. Mutation is the dangerous op: (a) never clear ro on a RECEIVED subvolume — permanently destroys Received UUID (only btrfs receive can set it) and leaves a fake-valid replica; (b) mutating an already-sent LOCAL parent silently desynchronizes source and target because btrfs send -p diffs against the local parent and never re-emits the change; nothing reports it. In-place purging of a large file is safe ONLY for snapshots that are neither send sources nor received (e.g. snapper's).

title: Reconcile scripts/ path drift between templates.rs and CMakeLists.txt (DAS_SCRIPT_DIR)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-23 during DAS-Backup-Manager-0p2 fix: indexer/src/setup/templates.rs lines 16, 282, 570 reference "${prefix}/lib/das-backup/scripts/" as the install path for production scripts, but CMakeLists.txt installs to DAS_SCRIPT_DIR=${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/lib/das-backup (no scripts/ subdir). Historical installs left both paths populated: real files at /usr/lib/das-backup/<name>.sh (canonical, where cmake installs) AND duplicates at /usr/lib/das-backup/scripts/<name>.sh (orphan).

Tonight (2026-05-23 23:19 CDT) I replaced the three orphan files (backup-run.sh, backup-verify.sh, boot-archive-cleanup.sh) under /usr/lib/das-backup/scripts/ with symlinks to ../<name>.sh as a short-term single-canonical-source patch. The deeper cleanup is to align the Rust code with cmake's install layout (or vice versa) so future re-installs do not regress.

Suggested approach: pick one canonical layout (cmake's flat /usr/lib/das-backup/ is cleaner) and update the templates.rs comments + test assertions + any production paths to match. Verify by reinstalling from clean state and checking only one copy lands on disk.

Cross-refs: DAS-Backup-Manager-0p2 (the trigger), .claude/rules/development-tools.md Single Canonical Source rule.

title: IndexBackupHistory signature mismatch: helper expects (sx), Qt passes positional s,x
description:
During the 2026-05-12 fix for DAS-Backup-Manager-29j, probing each of the six cascade methods on the now-running helper revealed that IndexBackupHistory's expected signature is reported by zbus as '(sx)' — a single struct argument of (string, int64) — not two positional args 's,x'.

The Qt call at gui/src/dbusclient.cpp:361 invokes the method as:
    m_interface->call(QStringLiteral("IndexBackupHistory"), dbPath, limit);

QDBusInterface::call() with positional args usually serializes to D-Bus signature 'sx' (two scalars), not '(sx)' (one struct). If this mismatch is real, the Backup History pane will throw a method-level error post-fix (the activation cascade hid this until now).

UNCONFIRMED: only running the GUI against the now-functional helper will reveal whether QDBusInterface auto-wraps positional args into a struct or whether the mismatch is genuine. If genuine, fix at either side:
  - Helper side: change the Rust signature to accept (s, x) as two positional args (likely a one-line zbus annotation change)
  - GUI side: pass the args wrapped in a QVariant/QDBusArgument that serializes to (sx)

Recommended: helper-side fix, so signature matches the GUI's natural calling convention.
close_reason: Not reproducible. User verified GUI works end-to-end 2026-05-12 — Backup History pane populates correctly, which means IndexBackupHistory succeeded. Qt's QDBusInterface::call() apparently auto-wraps positional (s, x) args into the (sx) struct signature zbus expects. zbus reporting '(sx)' on no-arg probe was misleading; not an actual signature mismatch.
